response.title: Acquire complete Kordloo2025 waste-aluminum-electrolyte bioleaching evidence
response.body:
The round64 lithium investigation verified the identity of Kordloo et al. (2025), *Lithium recovery from waste aluminum electrolyte via bioleaching: Comparative insights into acidic and alkaline pathways using Aspergillus niger and Glutamicibacter nicotianae*, DOI [10.1016/j.wasman.2025.115043](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wasman.2025.115043), PMID 40749529. This aluminum-production stream is a potential distinct secondary-resource owner, subject to full feed-provenance review.

The publisher preview and NCBI abstract do not establish complete methods or controls. The public publisher API returned core metadata only despite a full-text response wrapper; OpenAlex reported no accessible full text. No record, mechanism or CREATE history was admitted from abstract results. The source handoff is staged at `research/sources/round64-lithium/20261014T062345Z-source-investigation.{md,json}`; a permanent link will follow publication.

Acceptance work:

- Acquire the complete original article and relevant supplements through a legitimate accessible route; retain source URL, version, acquisition date and hashes.
- Verify the process generating the electrolyte waste and distinguish it from spent potlining, anodes, natural ores and battery black mass. Repeat hidden/ignored-inclusive material and study deduplication.
- Check strain/biomass identity, feed characterization, pretreatment, medium, loadings, pH, duration, replication, sterile and chemistry-matched controls, analytical fractions and denominator calculations.
- Inspect original plots, phase data and kinetic-fit limits. Preserve null results, contradictions and alternative chemical explanations; do not infer a molecular cause from a fitted kinetic model or isolated-product recovery from dissolved lithium.
- Curate only supported claims in the appropriate maintained owner, with canonical history, an independent exact-state scientific review and required validation. Otherwise retain an evidence-backed deferral.

This is a source-acquisition follow-up, not a defect in an accepted record. The documented deferral does not close the evidence gap. No author contact or paid access is requested.

response.title: Preserve the lepidocrocite study’s sterile-control curve in the record
response.body:
Independent round64 review found a minor omission in `data/records/lepidocrocite.yaml`: Figure 1 of O’Loughlin et al. (2019), DOI [10.3390/min9070434](https://doi.org/10.3390/min9070434), visibly includes a near-baseline sterile-control Fe(II) comparator. The record currently mentions no-donor cultures and a separate Pd/H2 surrogate but omits that curve.

The figure does not clearly specify donor/salt matching to the focused formate treatments. Its presence should be preserved without claiming a fully matched formate control or inventing an endpoint.

Immutable first observation: `reviews/structured/20261014T063915Z-lepidocrocite-round64-independent/review.yaml`, finding F1, issue key `lepidocrocite-2019-sterile-survey-control-omission`. Original locator: OSTI article PDF page 5, Figure 1. A permanent link will follow publication.

Acceptance:

- Add the qualitative near-baseline sterile-control curve and its exact figure locator.
- Retain the unresolved donor/salt matching and existing attribution limitations.
- Append correction history; preserve the initial review and save a successor covering the corrected bytes.
- Pass named validation, trusted-base history, affected batch checks and exact-state review coverage.

This is a supported curation correction, not a request to broaden the laboratory claim. The finding remains open until the fixing PR merges.
